transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because at work I keep leaving my station when I’m supposed to stay there. Like, I’ll just pop up or take off during meetings too, before I even really think about it. My supervisor said it’s becoming a safety problem, so… yeah, I figured I needed to get it checked out.
Has this kind of impulsive behavior been happening since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently?

No, it’s been going on since I was a kid. In elementary school I was always the one who couldn’t stay in my seat. I’d talk over the teacher, blurt things out, or just wander around the classroom, and I’d get notes sent home for it.
Do you also find it hard to focus or pay attention to tasks, like following instructions, staying organized, or finishing work?

Yeah, I do. Like when I’m doing inventory logs or trying to read the CNC training pages, I’ll start out really trying to focus, but after a few minutes the numbers or the words kind of blur together. Then I realize I didn’t actually take any of it in, so I have to go back and reread it or redo parts.
Do you also have trouble staying focused or feel restless in situations outside of work, like at home or when you're hanging out with friends?

Yeah, it’s not just at work. Even outside of work, if I’m supposed to just sit there or stand still, I get this feeling like pressure building up in my body. I feel like I have to move right then—pace around, stretch, get up, do something. It’s hard to just stay still.
Can you tell me if these issues with focus and restlessness also happen in other settings, like when you’re at home or in school if you’re taking classes?

Yeah, it happens in those kinds of situations too. Like if I’m trying to stand still by the machine or sit through training, I get this pressure building up in my body, like I need to move right away. I’ll end up pacing, stretching, or feeling like I have to go do something instead of just sitting or standing there.
